about: Ahmedabad-based IT infrastructure and IT managed services company serving mainly Government/PSU clients, which has also entered solar EPC, solar PPA and battery storage (BESS) projects and two Acer-branded Experience Zone retail stores. Revenue was about Rs 1,397 crore in FY26 with IT infrastructure making up 85.81% of it. It had 99 ongoing projects as of June 30, 2026.
sector: IT Infrastructure / IT Managed Services / Renewable Energy EPC

other.name: Revenue from Government/PSU incl. end-user Govt/PSU

objects.purpose: Funds for securing performance bank guarantees (PBGs) for expansion of business
Prepayment or repayment of certain outstanding borrowings
General corporate purposes (capped at 25% of issue proceeds)

promoters.background: Promoters have over two decades of experience in IT infrastructure and IT managed services, running the business earlier as a partnership firm (2003-2017). Experience in renewable energy is described as minimal.

concentration.note: Top five clients gave 76.66% of FY26 revenue; Government/PSU incl. end-user Government/PSU gave 83.84%; about 86% of revenue came from Gujarat, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

litigation_note: A cheque-dishonour case (Section 138 NI Act) over Rs 2.78 crore is pending against the company and its CMD, with a High Court stay, plus a related civil recovery suit. A collective labour grievance by contract staff in Gujarat alleges wage and statutory violations. Contingent liabilities were Rs 129.23 crore at Mar-26 (mostly Rs 126.15 crore of capital contracts).
strengths: Long track record of executing IT infrastructure projects for Government and PSU clients, with 116 Government/PSU projects completed in FY26.
Revenue grew from Rs 1,021 crore in FY24 to Rs 1,397 crore in FY26 while staying profitable every year, with PAT of Rs 45.47 crore in FY26.
Order book stood at Rs 1,196 crore at March 2026 and Rs 2,663 crore at June 2026, versus Rs 528 crore at March 2025.
Serves diverse sectors such as education, healthcare, public distribution and rural development, across 99 ongoing projects.
Returns remain high, with RoE of 28.52% and RoCE of 24.10% in FY26, though lower than earlier years.
Diversifying into solar EPC, solar PPA, BESS and retail Experience Zones to add new growth areas.
Experienced promoter-led management with over two decades in IT infrastructure.

risks.title: Heavy dependence on Government/PSU orders
risks.detail: 83.84% of FY26 revenue came from Government/PSU clients or projects where the end user is Government/PSU. Tender rule changes, delays or loss of eligibility could hurt revenue.

risks.title: High client concentration
risks.detail: Top five clients contributed 76.66% of FY26 revenue. Losing any big client or having a project cancelled would materially hurt earnings.

risks.title: Debt rising sharply
risks.detail: Borrowings rose from Rs 27.26 crore in FY24 to Rs 174.36 crore in FY26 and debt-equity from 0.29 to 0.96. Total borrowings including bank guarantees were Rs 318.55 crore at June 30, 2026. Promoter personal guarantees were Rs 398.85 crore.

risks.title: Negative or weak operating cash flow
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was negative Rs 17.98 crore in FY25 and only Rs 12.48 crore in FY26 against PAT of Rs 45.47 crore; business is working-capital intensive with large receivables of about Rs 513 crore.

risks.title: New and unproven renewable energy business
risks.detail: Renewable EPC contributed 8.93% of FY26 revenue and now forms most of the order book (51.71% EPC, 14.33% PPA, 22.35% BESS at June 2026). Promoters have minimal expertise in this sector.

risks.title: Falling bid success rate and margins
risks.detail: Bid success rate fell from 30.91% in FY24 to 19.48% in FY26. EBITDA margin was 5.42% and PAT margin 3.26% in FY26, versus 7.01% and 4.91% in FY24.

risks.title: Performance bank guarantees and tied-up funds
risks.detail: Company needs PBGs of 3% to 10% of project value backed by fixed deposits; Rs 124.37 crore of Rs 125.40 crore non-fund-based limits were used at March 2026, and Rs 155 crore of the issue is meant for PBGs.

risks.title: Related-party dealings and litigation
risks.detail: Significant dealings with promoter-linked entities including loans from promoters and related-party receivables, plus a pending cheque-dishonour case of Rs 2.78 crore and a contract-staff labour grievance. Promoters hold 92.72% pre-issue.

notes: Source: RHP, restated consolidated financials, Rs lakh converted to Rs crore. FY26 audited; June 2026 stub not used in arrays. Balance sheet table was garbled and was reconstructed using totals (cash_and_bank = cash and equivalents + other bank balances; reserves = other equity; borrowings = total debt as reported in KPI table; total assets and net worth tie out). Current ratio computed from reconstructed current assets/current liabilities (not reported in the RHP). EBITDA is as reported by the company (PBT + finance cost + D&A - other income). Price band, issue price, P/E and post-issue shares are blank in the RHP. Order book of Rs 2,663.44 crore is as of June 30, 2026 (Rs 1,196.06 crore at March 31, 2026). Reservation percentages are the regulatory minimums/maximums stated for the Net Issue (QIB not more than 25%, NII not less than 22.5%, retail not less than 52.5%); Issue is entirely a fresh issue of up to Rs 300 crore. Peer figures are as of August 20, 2026 prices; Oriana Power is listed on an SME board.
